==============================================================================
  MyCAD - Floor Plan Maker V15
==============================================================================

A simple program for drawing floor plans. With it you can:
  - draw walls and freehand lines, and take measurements
  - detect rooms automatically and calculate their area
  - work with several floors (walls of the floor below show through in gray)
  - add doors and windows to walls
  - place furniture and draw your own furniture pieces
  - view the house in 3D and export it as an OBJ file (Blender etc.)
  - manage furniture categories (add, rename, delete, reorder)
  - use metric (m/cm) or imperial (ft/in) units
  - choose a light or dark theme
  - use several languages (language files are in the lang/ folder)

Projects are saved as JSON files (File -> Save Project).
If you close the program or open another project while the drawing has
unsaved changes, MyCAD asks whether to save them first (Yes / No / Cancel).


------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  FILES AND FOLDERS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  mycad.pyw              The program
  lang/                  Language files (et.json, en.json, ...). Guide: lang/README.md
  check_translations.py  Checks translations and creates new language files
  requirements.txt       Requirements (no external packages needed)
  Info_EN.txt            This file (Estonian version: Info.txt)

On first start the program also creates these next to itself:
  config.json            Settings (language, units, theme, default wall height/thickness)
  library/               Furniture library. Each category is a separate JSON
                         file, and the list of categories is in
                         library/_categories.json

  error.log              Only appears if the program hits an error. Send this
                         file to the developer, since .pyw shows no console.

NOTE: These are always created in the program's own folder, so the program
must be in a folder you can write to, e.g. C:\Users\<name>\MyCAD, not
C:\Program Files.


------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  REQUIREMENTS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - Python 3.8 or newer
  - Tkinter (comes with Python, but on Linux it is often a separate package)

No other libraries are needed. All modules used (tkinter, json, math, os,
re, sys, shutil, time, unicodedata) are part of the Python standard library.


==============================================================================
  WINDOWS
==============================================================================

1) CHECK THAT PYTHON IS INSTALLED
   Open a command prompt (Win + R -> cmd -> Enter) and type:

       py --version

   If you see something like "Python 3.12.x", Python is installed.
   If you get an error, install Python from https://www.python.org/downloads/
   During installation select:
     [x] Add python.exe to PATH
     [x] tcl/tk and IDLE   (selected by default. This is Tkinter, keep it selected!)

2) CHECK TKINTER

       py -m tkinter

   If a small window opens saying "This is Tcl/Tk version ...", everything
   is in place. If you get "No module named tkinter", run the Python
   installer again, choose "Modify" and select "tcl/tk and IDLE".

3) RUN THE PROGRAM
   - Double-click mycad.pyw (no console window opens)
   - or from the command line, if you want to see possible error messages:

       cd C:\path\to\program\folder
       py mycad.pyw

4) BUILDING AN EXE (PyInstaller)
   Run these in the program folder:

       py -m pip install --upgrade pyinstaller
       py -m PyInstaller --onefile --windowed --name MyCAD --add-data "lang;lang" mycad.pyw

   The finished file is created at:  dist\MyCAD.exe

   What the options do:
     --onefile         packs everything into a single .exe file
     --windowed        no console window
     --add-data ...    bundles the language files. On first start they are
                       copied next to the exe into a lang\ folder, where you
                       can edit them and add new languages.
     --icon icon.ico   (optional) your own icon

   Notes:
     - The EXE must be built on Windows. You can't build a Windows exe on Linux.
     - If antivirus software flags the single-file exe (a false positive),
       use --onedir instead of --onefile. This creates a dist\MyCAD\ folder
       containing MyCAD.exe and its support files. Share the whole folder.
     - The temporary build\ folder and the MyCAD.spec file can be deleted afterwards.


==============================================================================
  LINUX
==============================================================================

1) CHECK THAT PYTHON AND TKINTER ARE INSTALLED

       python3 --version
       python3 -m tkinter

   If a small Tk window opens, everything is in place.
   If you get "No module named tkinter", install it:

       Debian / Ubuntu / Mint:   sudo apt install python3-tk
       Fedora:                   sudo dnf install python3-tkinter
       Arch / Manjaro:           sudo pacman -S tk
       openSUSE:                 sudo zypper install python3-tk

2) RUN THE PROGRAM

       cd /path/to/program/folder
       python3 mycad.pyw

3) STANDALONE PROGRAM (PyInstaller)
   Newer distros don't let pip install packages into the system Python,
   so use a virtual environment (venv):

       sudo apt install python3-venv python3-tk      # Debian/Ubuntu
       cd /path/to/program/folder
       python3 -m venv venv
       source venv/bin/activate
       pip install pyinstaller
       pyinstaller --onefile --windowed --name mycad --add-data "lang:lang" mycad.pyw
       deactivate

   The finished program is created at:  dist/mycad
   To run it:

       chmod +x dist/mycad
       ./dist/mycad

   Notes:
     - On Linux the --add-data separator is a colon (lang:lang),
       on Windows a semicolon (lang;lang).
     - The program runs on the same or a newer distro than the one it was
       built on. For the widest compatibility, build it on the oldest distro
       you want to support.
     - The temporary build/ and venv/ folders and the mycad.spec file can be
       deleted afterwards.

4) (OPTIONAL) MENU ENTRY
   Copy dist/mycad to e.g. ~/Apps/MyCAD/ and create the file
   ~/.local/share/applications/mycad.desktop with this content:

       [Desktop Entry]
       Type=Application
       Name=MyCAD
       Comment=Floor plan drawing
       Exec=/home/USERNAME/Apps/MyCAD/mycad
       Path=/home/USERNAME/Apps/MyCAD
       Terminal=false
       Categories=Graphics;


==============================================================================
  DOORS, WINDOWS AND 3D
==============================================================================

WALL HEIGHT AND THICKNESS
  - New walls are 260 cm high and 15 cm thick by default.
    You can change the defaults in Settings -> Wall Defaults.
  - Double-click a wall to open its properties. There you can change that
    wall's height and thickness, or apply them to all walls on the floor.
  - In 3D the floors are stacked: each floor is as high as its highest wall
    plus a 20 cm floor slab.

DOORS AND WINDOWS
  - Choose "Door" or "Window" on the toolbar (or in the furniture panel,
    category "Doors & Windows") and click a wall. The opening is placed where
    you click and always moves together with the wall. The tool stays active,
    so you can add several in a row. Choose "Select" when you are done.
  - In Edit mode you can drag a door or window along its wall.
  - Double-click a door or window to open its properties:
      door:   width, height, hinge side, swing direction
      window: width, height, sill height (how high the window starts)
  - R / L also changes the swing of the selected door.
  - Default sizes: door 90 x 210 cm, window 120 x 120 cm, sill 90 cm.
  - Doors placed as furniture symbols in older projects are turned into
    real wall openings automatically when the project is opened.

FURNITURE IN 3D
  - Built-in furniture has its own 3D shape and height (sofa, bed, table...).
  - Double-click a furniture piece to set its 3D height and its height above
    the floor (e.g. a wall cabinet).
  - The furniture creator has a "Height (3D)" field. The shape you draw is
    raised to that height in 3D.

DRAWING YOUR OWN FURNITURE ("+ New Furniture")
  - The drawing area is up to 5 x 5 m. There are rulers in centimetres at the
    top and left, and a red line on them shows where the cursor is.
  - "Grid": snap step of 1, 5 or 10 cm. It does not depend on the main
    program's grid.
  - Zoom: Ctrl + wheel or the - / + buttons. Wheel scrolls up/down,
    Shift + wheel sideways.
  - While drawing you see the shape's size (e.g. "60 x 40 cm") and the length
    of a polygon side. The whole piece has dimension lines next to it.
  - "Dimensions" box: Width, Depth and Height (3D). Type a width and depth
    and press Enter to resize the drawing to that size. If nothing is drawn
    yet, a rectangle of that size is created.
  - With the Select tool you can drag a shape to move it. For a polygon,
    click the points and double-click to finish.

SHELVES (storage shelf, bookcase ...)
  - The furniture panel has a ready "Storage shelf" (120 x 50 x 200 cm,
    5 boards) and a "Box" (60 x 40 x 30 cm) in the "Storage" category.
  - To make your own, choose "Type: Shelf" in the furniture creator and set
    "Shelf boards" (2-30) and "Lowest board from floor". Boards are spread
    evenly up to the piece's height (the top board is the shelf's top).
  - In 3D a shelf has posts and boards, so what you put in it is visible.
    In 2D it shows corner posts and a cross.
  - Put something onto a shelf (Stack on) and it goes to the lowest free
    board it fits on. If a box fits on top of another box without touching
    the next board it goes there, otherwise to the next board. Ctrl + D fills
    a shelf from the bottom up this way.
  - PageUp / PageDown moves the selected piece one board (or stack place)
    up or down.

SHELF VIEW (front view)
  - Double-click a shelf, or anything in it, to open its front view. The
    shelf is drawn to scale with its posts, boards and everything on them.
    Each board shows its free height (e.g. "↕ 44.5 cm"). Things further back
    are drawn paler.
  - Drag a piece sideways or onto another board. It never goes through a
    board or other pieces. If there is no room it is moved to the nearest
    free spot.
  - "Put on shelf": choose an item, press "Add" and click a board. The item
    is placed against the front edge. You can keep adding; Esc stops.
  - "Copy" (Ctrl + D) puts a copy next to it or in the next free spot.
    "Delete" (Del) deletes. "Properties" or double-click opens its properties.
  - The strip below shows the selected piece's board from above. Drag a
    piece up there to push it further back, or down to bring it forward.
  - Arrow keys move the selected piece 1 cm (Shift + arrow 5 cm). PageUp and
    PageDown move it one board up or down.
  - "View from the other side" looks at the shelf from its other side.
  - Every change shows up right away in the 2D plan and the 3D view.
  - Stairs automatically reach the next floor in 3D.

FURNITURE PANEL
  - Click a category header (e.g. "▼ Living Room (6)") to hide or show its
    items. "Collapse all" / "Expand all" does it for every category at once.
    The program remembers your choice for next time.

STACKING FURNITURE (e.g. a storage room)
  - When "Stack" is on in the toolbar (default), a piece you put or drag
    onto another piece goes on top of it automatically. "On top" means the
    centre of one piece is over the other one.
  - Ctrl + D copies the selected piece and puts the copy on top of it.
    Example, a stack of 8 boxes: place one box and press Ctrl + D 7 times.
  - Double-click a piece -> "Add copies on top (pcs)" adds several at once.
  - When you move away or delete a piece in a stack, the ones above drop down.
  - In 2D only the top piece of a stack shows its label, as "Box ×8", and
    ↑ shows how high above the floor it is. A click always picks the top piece.
  - If you type "Height above floor" by hand in the double-click dialog, the
    piece stays at that height (e.g. a wall cabinet) and doesn't drop.
  - To make your own piece (e.g. "Box"), use "+ New Furniture" and set its
    "Height (3D)" there.

3D VIEW (the "3D View" button)
  Left mouse + drag                  rotate around the house
  Right/middle mouse or Shift+drag   pan
  Mouse wheel or + / -               zoom
  Arrow keys                         rotate
  W / A / S / D                      move forward / left / back / right
  Q / E                              move down / up
  Shift + WASD / QE                  move faster
  "🚶 Walk mode"                     eye-level view (1.65 m) from the middle of a
                                     room: drag turns your head, wheel takes
                                     steps, walk from room to room with WASD
  "All floors"                       show all floors or only the current one
  "Furniture"                        show or hide furniture
  The 3D view updates by itself when you change the plan.

OBJ EXPORT
  File -> Export 3D (OBJ)... (or the same button in the 3D view)
  This creates house.obj and house.mtl (colours). Keep them in the same
  folder. Units are metres. The file opens in Blender, SketchUp (with a
  plugin), Windows 3D Viewer, MeshLab and many web viewers.


==============================================================================
  KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS
==============================================================================

  In the program press F1 (or ❓ Help -> Keyboard shortcuts) to open a
  window that lists all shortcuts by topic.

  F1                  show / close the keyboard shortcuts help

  R / L               rotate furniture clockwise / counter-clockwise
  Del                 delete selected
  Ctrl + click        add to selection
  Shift + click       remove from selection
  Drag on empty area  select multiple items
  Ctrl + scroll       zoom
  Middle mouse        pan the view
  M                   measuring tool
  Esc                 cancel current drawing
  Double-click        properties (wall, door, window, furniture)
  R / L (door)        change the swing of the selected door
  Ctrl + D            copy the selected furniture on top of itself
  PageUp / PageDown   move the selected piece one shelf / stack place up or down


==============================================================================
  ADDING A NEW LANGUAGE
==============================================================================

       py check_translations.py --new fi "Suomi"        (Windows)
       python3 check_translations.py --new fi "Suomi"   (Linux)

Then translate the values in lang/fi.json and check the result:

       py check_translations.py

In the program choose Settings -> Language -> "Reload language files".
For more details see lang/README.md.
